interest: This list of papers docket sheet offers a valuable index of U.S. and Allied economic intelligence-gathering on Japan's rubber industry and supply position across the critical transition from the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War to World War II (1937–1942). It illustrates the inter-agency and international exchange of strategic raw material intelligence, linking the State Department with domestic industry trade bodies (the Rubber Manufacturers Association), other executive agencies (the Department of Justice), and Allied partners (Great Britain). Additionally, the final entry from June 1942 underscores Allied analytical focus on critical manufacturing bottlenecks such as carbon black, revealing that even after Japan seized major Southeast Asian natural rubber plantations, its industrial rubber output remained vulnerable to shortages of essential compounding agents.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.6176, File 458) consists of a U.S. State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing four communications received between October 1937 and June 1942 relating to the Japanese rubber industry and rubber supplies. The indexed documents document American and Allied surveillance of Japan's strategic commodity position, spanning from the start of full-scale hostilities in China in 1937 through the early months of the Pacific War in 1942. The recorded papers include an October 1937 Tokyo Embassy despatch forwarding a review by the Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau, a November 1937 statement from the Rubber Manufacturers Association regarding Japanese crude rubber stocks, a November 1937 Department of Justice memorandum analyzing Japan's need for rubber, and a June 1942 despatch from Great Britain transmitting an intelligence report on the carbon black supply position in the Japanese rubber industry.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexing four documents from 1937 to 1942 concerning the Japanese rubber industry, crude rubber stocks, and carbon black supplies.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes four incoming communications filed under decimal file 894.6176 concerning Japan's rubber position between October 1937 and June 1942. The entries record an October 1937 Tokyo despatch enclosing a Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau review of the rubber industry, a November 1937 Rubber Manufacturers Association statement on crude rubber stocks in Japan, a November 1937 Justice Department memorandum regarding Japan's need for rubber, and a June 1942 British despatch transmitting a report on the carbon black supply position in the Japanese rubber industry. Together, these entries document U.S. and Allied monitoring of Japan's strategic raw material dependencies prior to and during World War II.
